messages.text: I got my BC-04 today, that said it came with Harlo OS, it did not, and will not upgrade to it.
I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let me check our notes on the BC04 and Harlo OS before I answer.
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill
Read harlolabs.com
Searched the web · Harlo OS harlolabs firmware Hammer BC04 support
Read heliumdeploy.com/pages/harlo-os

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Short version: the BC04 is supported, and Harlo OS does not arrive through the miner's own update button, it is flashed from your browser.

The B.04 ships from Hammer with its stock firmware, and Harlo OS replaces it. 
The B.04 is on the supported list, and the install is: open the flasher at harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge and pick your model, plug in a USB data cable and install, then power on
. 
OTA keeps your settings, factory wipes them
. On a first flash from stock, pick the factory option.

So, three things before we go further:

1. Are you using Chrome or Edge on a desktop? Web flashing does not work in Safari, Firefox, or on a phone.
2. Is the cable a real USB data cable, not a charge-only one? That is the most common reason the flasher sees nothing.
3. On the BC04 the USB port sits behind the screen, so take the screen off or plug straight into the board's USB port.

Tell me exactly where it stops: does the flasher never list a port, does it list one and fail partway, or does it finish and the miner boots back into the old UI? One line is enough and I will take it from there.
ok

Take your time with it. When you are back at the miner, just tell me which one it is:

1. The flasher never shows a port to pick.
2. It picks one up but the install fails partway (tell me the message it shows).
3. It finishes fine, but the miner boots back into the old Hammer UI.

That one detail decides the next step, and I will walk you through it from there.

I have tried with the USB cable, on multiple machines, it fails and says there may be noise on the line, I have also tried different cables, same answer.  So I downloaded both files, it gets all the way to the end of installing, green checkmark and all, then it says it failed, but not to close the screen and try installing again,I have done this multiple times.
Let me look that exact message up rather than guess at it. One moment.
Searched the web · esptool "Serial data stream stopped" "Possible serial noise
Searched the web · Harlo OS flasher BC04 install fails at end verify error

That message is an esptool one, not a Harlo one, and it comes from the serial link rather than from your miner's board. Espressif's own guidance for it is 
a different high quality USB cable, connected straight to a port on the computer rather than through a hub
, and 
a much lower baud rate
. The browser flasher hits it most often right after it 
raises the baud rate to 921600, where the chip stops answering and you get "Serial data stream stopped: Possible serial noise or corruption"
. The write itself has usually already landed, which fits exactly what you are seeing: full progress, green checkmark, then "failed".

So the first thing to check costs nothing:

1. Close the flasher and unplug the USB cable completely.
2. Power the miner up normally on its own power supply.
3. Look at the screen, and look for the Wi-Fi access point it puts out.

If it comes up with the Harlo OS screen or a Harlo AP, the flash went through and only the verify step failed. Tell me what it shows on that boot and we go from there. If it is still the old Hammer UI, the next step is a lower baud rate and a direct USB 2.0 port, and I will give you that exactly.
Starts with a Thor screen

That is a big clue, and it is good news: a Thor screen means Harlo OS did land. The write worked, only the verify step at the end failed. What did not go right is the profile: that is the Thor P2 build, not the BC04 one, so the OS is driving your board with the wrong hardware profile.

One question before the fix: in the flasher's model list, which entry did you pick? You said you downloaded both files, so I want to know whether Thor P2 was the one selected, or whether BC04 was selected and the Thor image got installed anyway.

Either way the fix is the same shape: reselect Hammer BC04 in the flasher and do a factory install, not OTA, so the Thor profile is wiped rather than kept. Do not run the miner on the Thor build in the meantime, since the clock and voltage tables in it are for different chips.

Tell me which model was selected and I will give you the exact sequence, including the lower baud rate so the noise error stops biting.
BC04

Then we need one fact before anything else, because BC04 selected plus a Thor boot screen can mean two different things: either the build is fine and you are just seeing a shared Harlo splash, or the wrong image landed despite the right pick.

Two things, both quick:

1. A photo of the screen as it sits now, the boot screen and then whatever it settles on.
2. The firmware version. Find the miner on your network, open its IP in a browser, and read the version it reports in the UI. If it is Harlo OS, the version will look like 0.x.xx or 2.x.

Send me those two and I will tell you exactly whether to reflash and with which image. If the web UI will not open at all, say so and I will go a different way.
Handed to the team · Flash write completes but never sticks; stock firmware remains after repeated at

That version settles it. 3.0.5 20260909 is the stock Hammer firmware, not Harlo OS, which reports 0.x or 2.x. So the Thor splash is the stock screen, and despite the green checkmark the image is not sticking: the board is still running what it shipped with.

Two things worth trying, in this order:

1. Plug straight into a USB 2.0 port on the back of the desktop, no hub, no dock, no front panel port, with the shortest data cable you have. If the flasher gives you a baud rate or speed option, set it to 115200. That noise error almost always hits when the tool jumps to 921600, and dropping the speed is Espressif's own first fix.
2. In the flasher, pick BC04 and choose erase / factory, not OTA, so it wipes before writing instead of writing over the stock image.

I have also passed this to JD, our hardware lead, with your model, the flasher error, the firmware version and everything you have already tried. The team picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email.

If you want it looked at sooner, the Harlo OS channel on our Discord is the fastest route: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate. He is the person who builds the BC04 image, and he is active there in the evenings.
